text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2: elevated SSE disconnect rate for streaming endpoints in us-west-2. Triggered by 5xxs and client connection resets. Paging on-call. See alert: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/1858001234 :pager:

Ben Hayes: I'm on it. Just started pulling logs for the last 30m. Initial metric: disconnect rate jumped from ~0.2% to 8% at ~01:12Z.

Clara Nguyen: thanks Ben. Any customer-facing errors? CS reported a drop in streaming completion events for two customers. @Dave Morales can you confirm impact?

Dave Morales: confirmed — two accounts (acct-472, acct-881) saw partial responses / truncated event streams starting ~01:13Z. One opened a support ticket. No PII exposure.

Erin Park: grabbing runtime traces. I'm seeing repeated `http2: stream reset` in router logs and `sse: connection closed by client` from edge. Also a bunch of tool-call parse failures around the same window: `tool-parser: malformed payload at offset 0x3f`. Posting sample logs below.

Ben Hayes: pasting tail of router logs (sensitive fields replaced):
```
[01:11:58Z] router-1 ERROR conn=0x8a4 reset reason=RST_STREAM code=2 path=/v1/stream
[01:12:01Z] router-3 WARN  conn=0x9ff read_timeout client=10.12.5.7
[01:12:12Z] router-2 ERROR conn=0xb34 reset reason=REFUSED_STREAM code=7 path=/v1/stream
[01:12:13Z] edge-1 INFO  sse conn_closed client_ip=3.5.2.1 reason=read-eof
[01:12:14Z] tool-parser ERROR malformed payload size=0x1a at conn=0xb34
```

Clara Nguyen: hmm. I also see a cluster-wide spike in CPU on the tool-runtime pods around 01:10-01:15Z. Might be correlated. Hypothesis A: a transient influx of large tool-call responses caused backpressure and connection resets. Hypothesis B: a client-side change triggering malformed SSE frames or chunking. Hypothesis C: proxy upgrade/rolling deploy caused intermittent incompatibility.

Frank Li: adding telemetry from model-serving — KV cache hit-rate dropped at same time; batching backlog increased. Could be increased per-request token lengths causing longer generation times and larger tool responses.

Ben Hayes: Mitigation applied: scaled tool-runtime replicas + temporarily increased connection timeouts on edge (from 30s -> 60s) at 01:20Z. Also enabled fallback to smaller model variant for dedicated customers at 01:23Z. Early telemetry shows disconnect rate down to ~1.6% by 01:30Z.

incident-bot: ACTION LOGGED: mitigation.scale.tool-runtime by ben.hayes at 01:20Z; mitigation.config.edge-timeout at 01:20Z; mitigation.fallback.model-variant at 01:23Z.

Alice Romero: on-call handoff incoming: I'm taking the next shift at 02:30Z. Ben, please summarize open action items for the handoff.

Ben Hayes: open items: 1) collect full tool-runtime heap profiles from 00:50-01:40Z (Erin). 2) synth reproducer for malformed tool-call payload (Frank/Alice). 3) timeline + correlate deploys in infra (Clara). 4) customer outreach draft (Dave).

Erin Park: heap profiles and traces uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/1858001234/profiles.tar.gz. Key traces show GC spikes and continuous blocking syscalls in tool-runtime worker 4.

Frank Li: started a local reproduction with larger tool outputs (5-10x typical size) — seeing that our stream chunker sometimes emits a zero-length chunk when content-length differs from chunk framing; reproducer scripts in gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro-1858001234.

Clara Nguyen: checking deploy logs: no infra deploys targeting edge/router clusters between 00:00 and 02:00Z. There was a config push to firewall rules at 00:58Z but it was non-disruptive and rolled back at 01:00Z. Not correlated.

Dave Morales: customer comms ready to send once we confirm root cause. Draft: "We observed transient streaming interruptions... mitigations applied... next steps..." I'll hold until handoff.

Ben Hayes: hypothesis tracker (informal in-thread):
- H1 (backpressure): tool-runtime overloaded by unexpectedly large tool responses -> increased latency -> edge timeouts -> client resets. Evidence: CPU + GC spikes, batching backlog, reproducer shows zero-length chunk on heavy payloads.
- H2 (client-side change): clients started sending malformed chunked payloads -> parser errors. Evidence for: `malformed payload` logs, but unclear if synthetic. Need customer payloads to verify.
- H3 (protocol mismatch): recent stream-chunker change causes rare zero-length chunk emission when combined with large tool outputs. Evidence: reproducer and chunker code path touched in last minor release 2026-02-10.

Alice Romero: for handoff: I'll take H1 and H3 as highest priority to validate. Plan: run canary with stricter chunk validation on tool-runtime and deploy patched chunker to a single node, watch for parser errors. If errors disappear -> H3.

Erin Park: flags/notes for handoff: keep fallback model variant and increased timeouts until root cause confirmed. If we rollback the chunker patch, we should also disable strict validation to avoid false positives.

incident-bot: REACTION: :white_check_mark: mitigation.stable observed at 01:36Z (disconnect rate down to 1.4%).

Ben Hayes: timeline notes I'm adding to the public incident doc: 00:58Z firewall config push (no impact), 01:10Z disconnect rate starts rising, 01:12Z spike, 01:20Z scaled tool-runtime and increased timeouts, 01:23Z enabled smaller model fallback, 01:36Z metrics improving. I'll assemble a fuller timeline with graph links.

Frank Li: pushed a proto-fix branch for the chunker with stricter chunk-length checks: branch `fix/chunker-validate-1858`. Running unit + integration tests now.

Alice Romero: taking over oncall at 02:30Z. I'll monitor alerts and coordinate with Clara/Frank for the canary. Dave, please go ahead with the customer note: keep it factual, no blame.

Dave Morales: sending customer note now. Copying draft here: "We observed intermittent streaming interruptions; we applied mitigations (scaled services, increased timeouts, temporary fallback). We're investigating root cause; we'll follow up with technical details and timeline"

Clara Nguyen: next steps for RCA: 1) merge reproducer and confirm chunker failure mode, 2) run canary patch on a single tool-runtime node, 3) collect 2 hours of post-patch telemetry, 4) if patch clears parser errors, schedule wider rollout.

Ben Hayes: thanks team. Closing immediate pager for now — continuing investigation. I'll tag updates in this thread.

Alice Romero: acknowledged. Handoff complete. I'll post a summary after the canary.

incident-bot: THREAD STATUS: investigating -> monitoring.
